chunks: And Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara from Isa ibn Abdillah from his father from his grandfather from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said one day while we were with him: 'When someone comes to you whose character and religion you approve, then marry him.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, even if he is lowly in lineage?' He said: 'When someone comes to you whose character and religion you approve, then marry him. Indeed, if you do not do so, there will be fitnah (trial/strife) in the earth and great corruption.'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary criterion for marriage in Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on Kafa'ah (compatibility) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam emphasizes that piety and character outweigh noble lineage, a key Shia principle for social cohesion. The Prophet’s warning that neglecting this leads to 'fitnah and great corruption' underscores the societal instability caused by rigid class exclusivity in marriage. This teaching aligns with the Shia scholarly view that spiritual merit is the primary criterion for marital compatibility.
